\[
PC_o(x) = W_o(x)\, \frac{\max\!\big(\sum_s A_{s}(x) \big(\cos(\phi_{s} - \bar\phi) - \lvert \sin(\phi_{s} - \bar\phi) \rvert\big) - T,\ 0\big)}{\sum_s A_{s}(x) + \varepsilon}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(A_s, \phi_s\): The amplitude and phase of the filter response at scale s
- \(\bar\phi\): The phase of the summed responses
- \(T\): The noise threshold
- \(W_o\): The weight for the spread of the frequencies

Phase congruency asks whether the Fourier components of the image agree in phase at a point. At a step or a line they all do, whatever the contrast. Each direction o has a bank of log-Gabor filters at several scales s. Each filter gives an even and an odd response, with the amplitude A_s and the phase phi_s. The energy sums A_s (cos(phi_s - phi_mean) - |sin(phi_s - phi_mean)|), so it is large where the phases agree with their weighted mean. The noise threshold T is subtracted. Kovesi estimates it from the smallest scale, as the mean plus k standard deviations of a Rayleigh distribution. Dividing by the sum of the amplitudes removes the contrast, and a sigmoid weight W_o lowers points where only a few scales respond. The vectors PC_o (cos theta_o, sin theta_o) of all directions form a covariance matrix. Its largest moment M is high on edges and its smallest moment m on corners. The feature type is the angle between the summed even and odd responses.
